# Bot Admin → Cabinet Admin Parity Gap Report

What the **Telegram bot admin panel** can do that the **web cabinet admin** (backend API + React frontend) cannot. 27 domains audited. This is your build list.

---

## 1. Executive Summary

**Overall state:** The cabinet has solid-to-superset parity on the *CRUD-heavy commercial domains* (campaigns, promocodes, tariffs, channels, updates, broadcasts, partners/withdrawals) but is missing **entire operational/maintenance subsystems** that exist only in the bot. The pattern of the gaps is consistent: the cabinet covers "manage entities" well, and is weak on "operate the running system" (monitoring, maintenance runtime, backups, logs, receipt reconciliation, referral repair) and on a handful of growth/engagement features (contests, polls, welcome text, user-menu messages, FAQ).

**Domains by status (27 total):**

| Status | Count | Domains |
|---|---|---|
| **Full parity (cabinet ≥ bot)** | 5 | campaigns, promocodes, required_channels, updates, *(plus tariffs near-full)* |
| **Partial — needs work** | 13 | users, remnawave, bot_configuration, tariffs, promo_offers, broadcasts_messages, referrals_partners, promo_groups, pricing, tickets_support, servers, payments, statistics_reports_trials |
| **Mostly missing** | 4 | monitoring, ban_blacklist, policies_offer_rules, maintenance, backup |
| **Entirely missing** | 6 | contests, polls, faq, welcome_text, system_logs *(+ user_menu_messages sub-domain)* |

**The biggest gaps (start here):**
1. **Contests** (referral + daily game) — a whole ~30-action admin subsystem, zero cabinet coverage, both layers.
2. **Monitoring / NaloGO receipts / win-back notifications** — operational core entirely absent; includes financially-sensitive tax-receipt reconciliation.
3. **Backup operations** — create/list/restore/upload-restore all bot-only; restore is your disaster-recovery path.
4. **Maintenance runtime control** — the cabinet edits the *wrong* maintenance flag; it cannot actually turn maintenance on/off at runtime.
5. **Referral repair tooling** — detect & retroactively pay un-credited bonuses; financially significant, bot-only.
6. **Polls, Welcome text, User-menu messages, FAQ, Legal docs editing, System logs** — fully bot-only engagement/content/ops features.

A recurring sub-pattern worth noting: in several "partial" domains (remnawave, servers, tariffs, referrals) **the cabinet backend endpoint already exists but no frontend wires it up** — those are cheap, high-value wins.

## 2. Entirely Missing in Cabinet (bot-only, build both layers)

These have **no cabinet admin route and no cabinet admin page** at all.

### 2.1 Contests (HIGH) — `app/handlers/admin/contests.py` + `daily_contests.py`
Two sub-systems, ~30 admin actions, zero cabinet coverage (cabinet `contests.py`/`Contests.tsx` are user-side play only).
- **Referral contests:** list/paginate, create (FSM wizard: mode paid-vs-registered, title, desc, prize, start/end datetime, daily-summary times, timezone), detail view, toggle active, edit summary times, delete (finished only), leaderboard top-10, **detailed per-participant stats** (invited/paid/unpaid/amount, subscription vs deposit totals), **sync with real payments** (reconcile out-of-period events), debug transactions, and **virtual "ghost" participants** (list/add/edit/delete + bulk "массовка" generate).
- **Daily game contests (templates):** list templates w/ enabled+prize+max-winners, detail (prize type/value, attempts/user, rounds/day, schedule, cooldown), toggle enabled, edit all fields, edit raw JSON payload, **start round now / manual-test start / start-all**, **close round / close-all**, reset attempts / reset-all.
- **Build:** new `admin_contests.py` (+ daily sub-routes), new `AdminContests*.tsx` pages. Largest single body of work. *Note: gated by `CONTESTS_ENABLED`; only build if enabled in target deployments.*

### 2.2 Polls (HIGH) — `app/handlers/admin/polls.py`
Cabinet `polls.py`/`Polls.tsx` are user-participation only; no admin layer at all.
- List polls (admin catalog), **create poll** (title, HTML desc, reward amount, multi-question with ordered options), view full poll structure, **send/distribute to audience** (~8 segments + ~8 custom criteria + recipient-count preview + sent/failed/skipped report), **statistics** (invited/completed/reward-paid + per-question per-option counts), delete, configure completion reward.
- **Build:** new `admin_polls.py` + `AdminPolls*.tsx`. Audience-targeting helpers already exist (broadcasts reuse them).

### 2.3 Welcome Text (HIGH) — `app/handlers/admin/welcome_text.py`
Post-registration welcome message editor. **Caveat:** a token-auth `app/webapi/routes/welcome_texts.py` exists but is NOT the cabinet API and the frontend never calls it, and it lacks validation/preview.
- View panel + on/off status, toggle enabled, view current text, **edit with validation** (10–4000 chars, Telegram-HTML whitelist, `<a href>` scheme check, tag pairing), reset to default, **live preview with placeholder substitution**, placeholders help, formatting help.
- **Build:** new cabinet route over `WelcomeText` model + `AdminWelcomeText.tsx`. (Could wrap the existing webapi logic but must add the bot's validation.)

### 2.4 User-Menu Messages (HIGH) — `app/handlers/admin/user_messages.py` *(sub-domain of broadcasts)*
Messages shown inside the user main menu (between subscription info and action buttons), shown at random. Entirely absent — no backend route, no page.
- Add (HTML-validated, max 4000), list (paginated, status icon, preview), view, edit text, toggle active/inactive, delete, stats (total/active/inactive).
- **Build:** new `admin_user_messages.py` + `AdminUserMessages.tsx`.

### 2.5 FAQ — bot's `faq_pages` (HIGH) — `app/handlers/admin/faq.py`
**Architectural trap:** the cabinet's `admin_info_pages.py`/`AdminInfoPages.tsx` is a **different table** (`info_pages`, JSONB multilingual) and does NOT touch the bot's `faq_pages`/`faq_settings`. The cabinet only *reads* `faq_pages` for end users (`info.py`). So the bot's FAQ content is unmanageable from the cabinet.
- Per-language FAQ page CRUD (create/edit title/edit content/delete), toggle page active, **global enable/disable per language**, reorder up/down with display_order renormalize, Telegram-HTML validation + help.
- **Build decision:** either (a) add cabinet admin routes/UI over `faq_pages`+`faq_settings`, or (b) **consolidate the two FAQ systems onto one table** (recommended — two parallel FAQs that don't sync is a confusion risk).

### 2.6 System Logs (HIGH/MED) — `app/handlers/admin/system_logs.py`
Raw runtime log file viewing. **Trap:** cabinet `admin_audit_log.py`/`AdminAuditLog.tsx` is the RBAC *audit* log (who-did-what), NOT the application log.
- **View** raw `bot.log` tail with path/size/last-modified metadata (HIGH), refresh/live re-read (MED), **download** full log file (HIGH).
- **Build:** new cabinet route that tails+streams `settings.LOG_FILE` (with permission gating + sanitization) + `AdminSystemLogs.tsx`.

## 3. Partial / Needs Work (present but incomplete)

### 3.1 Monitoring (mostly_missing) — backend AND frontend
Only the *config keys* (TRAFFIC_*, MONITORING_INTERVAL) are editable via generic settings. All operational control is bot-only. **Zero** `monitoring_service`/`NotificationSettingsService`/NaloGO references in cabinet.
- **both / HIGH:** Start/Stop monitoring loop; Force-check subscriptions now; **NaloGO receipt queue** (view/force-process/pending-verify/mark-verified/retry/clear-all); **receipt reconciliation** (payments-missing-receipts report from log parsing); **user expiry/win-back notification settings** (enable trial-channel/expired_1d/2nd-wave/3rd-wave + edit discount %/hours/trigger-day — stored in `data/notification_settings.json`, outside the settings system the cabinet reads).
- **both / MED:** Monitoring dashboard/status view; manual traffic-delta check; monitoring logs view; link-old-YooKassa-to-NaloGO; consolidated monitoring page.
- **both / LOW:** clear logs; statistics screen; send test/preview notifications.

### 3.2 Maintenance (mostly_missing) — backend AND frontend
**Critical architectural finding:** cabinet edits `settings.MAINTENANCE_MODE` (config flag) via generic settings, but `cabinet/dependencies.py` actually blocks users based on `maintenance_service.is_maintenance_active()` (runtime singleton). Editing the config key does NOT flip the runtime flag — so the cabinet **cannot actually turn maintenance on/off**.
- **both / HIGH:** Runtime maintenance toggle (enable-with-reason/disable) that calls `maintenance_service.enable/disable`; runtime status dashboard; start/stop API-monitoring loop.
- **both / MED:** force Remnawave connectivity check (with auto-recover); rich panel-health summary (online/degraded, response time, users/nodes online); send manual status notification (online/offline/degraded/maintenance + message).

### 3.3 Backup (mostly_missing) — backend AND frontend
Only BACKUP config keys are editable via generic settings. No `admin_backup.py`, no `adminBackup.ts`, no `AdminBackup.tsx`.
- **both / HIGH:** Create on-demand backup; list backups w/ metadata + pagination; delete backup; **restore from backup (append + wipe-then-restore)**; **upload-and-restore** a backup file.
- **both / MED:** view per-backup detail (tables/records/compressed/errors).

## 6. Caveats (verify by hand before building)

1. **Maintenance two-flag trap (verify).** The audit asserts `system_settings_service.set_value()` (the cabinet PUT path) writes `settings.MAINTENANCE_MODE` but has **no side-effect** calling `maintenance_service.enable/disable`. Confirm this — if true, editing maintenance in the cabinet today is cosmetic and does nothing at runtime. This determines whether item #1 is "wire a side-effect" (S) or "new endpoint" (M).

2. **`/sync/auto/toggle` is a stub (verify).** Audit says the remnawave auto-sync toggle backend "does not persist `REMNAWAVE_AUTO_SYNC_ENABLED`, only refreshes/logs." Item #50 needs the backend fixed before the frontend toggle is meaningful.

3. **Two FAQ systems (decision required).** `faq_pages`/`faq_settings` (bot, per-language rows) vs `info_pages` (cabinet, JSONB multilingual). They don't sync. Confirm there's no migration already underway, then decide: mirror the bot's table, or consolidate. This is an architecture call, not just a feature.

4. **CONTESTS_ENABLED gate.** Referral contests are gated by `CONTESTS_ENABLED`. Confirm how many deployments actually run contests before committing to the XL build (#17) — it may be lower priority than its severity suggests if rarely enabled.

5. **Welcome-text webapi overlap.** There's an existing `app/webapi/routes/welcome_texts.py` (token-auth, no validation). Verify whether to reuse its model/logic in the new cabinet route — but the cabinet version MUST add the bot's HTML/length validation and the preview/placeholder/help screens, which the webapi lacks.

6. **Notification settings storage.** Win-back/expiry notification settings live in `data/notification_settings.json` via `NotificationSettingsService`, NOT in `BotConfiguration`. The cabinet's generic settings page can't reach them. Confirm the JSON-file store is concurrency-safe before exposing writes over a web API (file-based mutation from a web request needs locking).

7. **Promo-offer "correctness" gap (#31) is not cosmetic.** The cabinet's `/broadcast` reuses generic segmentation and loses the test_access "already has squad" skip — so it can blast offers to users who already own the squad and to forbidden segments. Verify the exact segment lists in `get_users_for_promo_segment` vs `get_target_users` before reimplementing.
